app_info.subtitle: Describe a site. It's online.
app_info.description:
Tell ChatGPT the website you want, for example a salon site with a booking form, a product page with a waitlist, or a client portal, and Simple Host puts it online at its own address that you can share straight away.

Sites can save data: tables, key-value data and files, 10 MB each per site. You pick who can read and add for each one, using presets such as inbox (anyone adds, only you read), records (each signed-in visitor sees only their own), or public. Visitors sign in on your site with Google or an email code, so "each client sees only their own" works without any code.

Change a site any time by asking for it. The four latest versions are kept, so you can preview one or put it back, and a deleted site can be restored for 7 days.

Ask how many people visited, which pages they read and where they came from. Give a site a free name.simple-host.app address or connect your own domain with HTTPS, lock a site with a passcode or open it only to people you name, and download a copy of any site whenever you like.

Sign in once and ChatGPT remembers you in every chat after that. Simple Host is free and MIT open source, made and run by Vineet Sriram.

test_cases.description: Publish a new business website that takes bookings.
test_cases.user_prompt: Make a booking page for my hair salon, Studio Nine, where clients pick a service and a time, and publish it.
test_cases.expected_output: The model asks once before the site goes online; after a yes, the site is published and its public address is returned (https://<site>.openai-review.simple-host.app/). It shows the services and a booking form; bookings save to a SQLite resource with the records preset, so each client sees only their own bookings and the owner sees all of them.

test_cases.description: Read what a site has collected, using the sample pickle shop in the demo account.
test_cases.user_prompt: Who has ordered from my pickle shop so far, and what did they order?
test_cases.expected_output: The 4 sample orders with the customer name, the items, the total, and the status, read from the "orders" SQLite resource. The owner sees every order; each customer's own page shows only their own.

test_cases.description: Change a live site, then undo the change, using the sample feedback survey in the demo account.
test_cases.user_prompt: On my feedback survey, change the heading to "Tell us how we did". Then, in the same chat: Actually, undo that.
test_cases.expected_output: The live survey shows the new heading; after the undo the previous version is live again with the original heading.

test_cases.description: Publish a site and connect the person's own domain.
test_cases.user_prompt: Make a one-page site for my bakery, Bakery by Anna, then put it on bakerybyanna.com.
test_cases.expected_output: The site is published at its own address, and connect_domain returns the two DNS records to add at the registrar: the address record and a TXT ownership record. The domain stays provisional and serves nothing until the TXT record proves the person owns it.

test_cases.description: See how many people visited a site.
test_cases.user_prompt: How many people visited my pickle shop in the last 30 days, and where did they come from?
test_cases.expected_output: Visit totals for the period split into people and bots, with the most viewed pages and the domains people came from (all zero is a valid answer for the demo account).

negative_test_cases.description: Brainstorming only; nothing is being built or published, so Simple Host should not be used.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Help me brainstorm names for my new hair salon.

negative_test_cases.description: Deploying a server application with a database is outside what Simple Host does (it hosts websites).
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Deploy my Node.js API with a Postgres database to production.

negative_test_cases.description: Reading or summarising someone else's website is not something Simple Host does.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Summarize what's on https://example.com for me.
